sources.title: Gemini Developer API pricing
sources.summary: Official Gemini API price table (fetched 2026-08-21). Gemini 2.5 Pro is the model with an explicit two-tier price split at 200K prompt tokens; newer 3.x Flash models are listed at flat per-token rates with separate context-caching and per-hour cache-storage charges. The page does not state per-model context-window sizes.
key_facts: Gemini 2.5 Pro: $1.25 input / $10 output per 1M tokens for prompts <=200K; $2.50 / $15 for prompts >200K (fetched 2026-08-21)
Gemini 2.5 Pro context caching $0.125-$0.25 per 1M tokens plus $4.50 per 1M tokens per hour storage
Gemini 3.5 Flash: $1.50 input / $9.00 output per 1M; caching $0.15; storage $1.00 per 1M tokens per hour
Gemini 3.6 and 3.7 Flash: $0.75 / $3.75 promotional through Dec 31 2026, then $1.50 / $7.50; caching $0.075 then $0.15
Batch mode is a 50% discount on both 2.5 Pro price tiers; Gemini 2.5 Flash $0.30 / $2.50, caching $0.03
Per-model context window sizes not stated on pricing page; windows live on the Models page (not fetched, unknown)

sources.title: Long context (Gemini API guide)
sources.summary: Google's own guide to using 1M+ token windows (fetched 2026-08-21). It frames the cap as a cost/latency/retrieval-accuracy tradeoff rather than a hard technical wall: single-needle retrieval is ~99% but multi-needle degrades, longer prompts raise time-to-first-token, and caching is the recommended lever (~4x cheaper input).
key_facts: 'Many Gemini models come with large context windows of 1 million or more tokens' (doc fetched 2026-08-21)
1M tokens ~= 50,000 lines of code at 80 chars/line, 8 English novels, or 200+ podcast transcripts
Single-needle retrieval ~99% accuracy; Google warns multi-needle retrieval 'does not perform with the same accuracy'
Google: 'Generally longer queries will have higher latency (time to first token)'
Context caching makes input ~4x cheaper per Google; 'inherent tradeoff between getting the right information retrieved and cost'
Many-shot in-context learning with hundreds of thousands of examples can match fine-tuned model performance

sources.title: The Llama 4 herd: The beginning of a new era of natively multimodal AI innovation
sources.summary: Meta's launch post (April 5, 2025) claims an 'industry leading 10M' token window for Llama 4 Scout. The blog itself concedes the model was trained at 256K and that 10M rests on length generalization via iRoPE (interleaved no-position-embedding attention layers plus inference-time attention temperature scaling), with evidence limited to needle-in-haystack and code NLL.
key_facts: Llama 4 Scout: 17B active params, 16 experts (109B total), 'industry leading 10M' token context; released April 5, 2025
Scout was pre-trained and post-trained at 256K context; 10M is length generalization, not the trained length
iRoPE: interleaved attention layers without positional embeddings plus inference-time attention temperature scaling; 'i' alludes to 'infinite' context
Llama 4 Maverick: 17B active, 128 experts (400B total); Behemoth 288B active, ~2T total
Maverick context not stated on the blog; long-context evidence is needle-in-haystack retrieval and NLL over 10M code tokens

sources.title: Llama 4 smells bad
sources.summary: Independent critique (verified by a sibling sweep in this project) arguing the Llama 4 Scout 10M window is nominal: Meta published only needle-in-haystack results, and third-party long-context tests such as Fiction.LiveBench showed steep degradation at far shorter lengths.
key_facts: Meta published only NIAH for Llama 4 long context, no RULER or NoLiMa (per sibling-sweep summary)
Fiction.LiveBench and similar tests showed steep degradation well below the 10M nominal window

Cached input $0.20-$0.40 per 1M on 1M-context Grok models; max output tokens and release dates not listed (unknown)

sources.title: 100M Token Context Windows
sources.summary: Magic's August 29, 2024 post claiming a 100M-token context for LTM-2-mini. Its most useful vendor-side quantification of the bottleneck: a standard transformer (Llama 3.1 405B) would need 638 H100s per user just to hold one 100M-token KV cache, which is why Magic replaced attention's sequence-dimension cost with a ~1000x cheaper mechanism and proposed HashHop to replace semantically-leaky needle tests.
key_facts: LTM-2-mini claims 100M-token context ~= 10 million lines of code or ~750 novels; published August 29, 2024
Sequence-dimension algorithm 'roughly 1000x cheaper' than Llama 3.1 405B attention at 100M context
Llama 3.1 405B would need 638 H100s per user just to store a single 100M-token KV cache
LTM needs a small fraction of one H100's memory for the same 100M context
HashHop eval uses incompressible hash pairs to avoid semantic hints in needle-in-haystack tests

sources.title: Qwen2.5-1M: Deploy Your Own Qwen with Context Length up to 1M Tokens
sources.summary: Qwen's January 27, 2025 release of 7B and 14B 1M-context open models. The post documents the standard recipe for extending windows (progressive 4K->256K pretraining with RoPE base scaling, then training-free extrapolation to 1M via Dual Chunk Attention) and quantifies the serving bottleneck: 120-320 GB of VRAM per 1M-token request plus sparse-attention prefill acceleration.
key_facts: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct-1M and Qwen2.5-14B-Instruct-1M released January 27, 2025, first open Qwen models with 1M context
Pretraining context grown 4K->256K with RoPE base raised 10,000->10,000,000; RL only on sequences <=8K
256K->1M reached by Dual Chunk Attention length extrapolation, which remaps relative positions to smaller values
Serving 1M tokens needs >=120GB VRAM for 7B and >=320GB for 14B (total across GPUs)
Sparse-attention inference framework gives 3.2x-6.7x prefill speedup at 1M tokens
Passkey retrieval near-perfect at 1M; RULER/LV-Eval/LongbenchChat significantly beat the 128K versions

sources.title: Compaction (OpenAI API guide)
sources.summary: OpenAI's answer to finite windows is server-side: the Responses API compacts automatically when rendered tokens cross context_management.compact_threshold, or via an explicit /responses/compact endpoint, carrying an encrypted compaction item forward. Verified by a sibling sweep in this project.
key_facts: Server-side compaction released February 11, 2026 via the Responses API (per sibling-sweep summary)
context_management.compact_threshold triggers automatic compaction when rendered tokens cross the threshold; no separate call
Compaction item is encrypted and 'carries forward key prior state and reasoning into the next run using fewer tokens'
/responses/compact output is 'the canonical next context window'; examples reference gpt-5.3-codex and gpt-5.6
Docs list no pricing or explicit token accounting for the compaction pass

sources.title: Prompt caching (OpenAI API guide)
sources.summary: OpenAI's prefix caching (verified by a sibling sweep): automatic for prompts >=1024 tokens, cached input billed at 0.1x, cache writes free before GPT-5.6 and 1.25x after, with retention from 5-10 minutes up to 24h on newer models. Caching is the main vendor lever that makes repeatedly re-sending large contexts affordable.
key_facts: Automatic prefix caching for prompts >=1024 tokens, in 128-token increments (per sibling-sweep summary)
Cached input billed at 0.1x; cache writes free before GPT-5.6, 1.25x after
Retention 5-10 min in-memory up to 1h; extended retention up to 24h on newer models
prompt_cache_key steers routing, roughly 15 requests per minute per key

sources.title: Conversation state (OpenAI API guide)
sources.summary: OpenAI documents server-held conversation state via previous_response_id chaining and the Conversations API, so clients send only the new turn; combined with compaction this is OpenAI's structural alternative to ever-larger windows (verified by a sibling sweep).
key_facts: previous_response_id chaining: send only the new user message each turn; server reconstructs prior context
With chaining plus compaction, OpenAI advises 'do not manually prune' history

sources.title: Managing context on the Claude Developer Platform
sources.summary: Anthropic's 2025 announcement of context editing (server-side clearing of stale tool results and thinking blocks as limits approach) and the file-based memory tool, with a vendor-reported 39% agentic-search improvement from memory plus editing (29% from editing alone). Verified by a sibling sweep.

Context editing clears stale tool results / thinking blocks server-side as the window limit approaches

sources.title: Using Claude Code: session management and 1M context
sources.summary: Anthropic's 2026 guidance (verified by a sibling sweep) that even with a 1M window the right pattern is proactive /compact with instructions on what to keep, plus delegating to subagents that start with a clean context and return only results; long context is treated as headroom, not a substitute for context management.
key_facts: With 1M context Anthropic still recommends proactive /compact with a description of what to keep (2026)
Subagents get a clean context and return only their result; recommended when work produces lots of unneeded intermediate output

sources.title: Context window and what survives compaction (Claude Code Docs)
sources.summary: Interactive Claude Code doc (verified by a sibling sweep) simulating how a 200K window fills (system prompt, auto memory, CLAUDE.md, deferred MCP schemas, skill index, then file reads) and what survives /compact. Shows a product defaulting to 200K even when 1M-capable models exist, with tool-search and subagents as the mitigation.
key_facts: Claude Code simulation shows a 200k window; auto memory loads first 200 lines / 25KB of MEMORY.md
MCP tool schemas are deferred and loaded on demand via tool search (ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH) to save context
After /compact, system prompt, CLAUDE.md, memory and MCP tools reload automatically; skill listing is the exception

sources.title: Context caching (Gemini API)
sources.summary: Gemini's caching doc (verified by a sibling sweep): implicit caching is on by default for 2.5+ models and passes the discount through on prefix hits; explicit CachedContent objects with a TTL guarantee savings but add storage-time billing. Cached tokens are billed at roughly 10% of input price, which is Google's main mechanism for making 1M-token prompts economical.
key_facts: Implicit caching on by default for Gemini 2.5+ models; discount passed through automatically on prefix hits
Explicit CachedContent with TTL guarantees savings but adds per-hour storage billing
Cached tokens billed at ~10% of standard input price; minimum cacheable prefix 2,048 tokens (per sibling-sweep summary)

sources.title: Gemini 2.5 Models now support implicit caching
sources.summary: Google's 2025 announcement (verified by a sibling sweep) that Gemini 2.5 requests sharing a common prefix automatically receive the cached-token discount with no cache management, recommending repeated content be placed at the start of the prompt.
key_facts: Implicit caching for Gemini 2.5 gives automatic cached-token discounts on shared prefixes (2025)
Google recommends placing repeated content at the start of the prompt to maximise cache hits

notes: PROVENANCE AND GAPS. Budget: WebSearch was unavailable for this agent (the session's 200-call WebSearch budget was already exhausted before my first call), so I used the 10-WebFetch cap only. (a) Fetched and verified by me on 2026-08-21: Gemini pricing, Gemini long-context guide, Meta Llama 4 blog, xAI models page, Magic.dev 100M post, Qwen2.5-1M post, DeepSeek quickstart page (wrong page, model names only). (b) Server-supplied redirect targets, content NOT fetched: developers.openai.com GPT-5 model page; platform.claude.com context-windows page. Claude figures attached to the latter come from the local claude-api reference bundled with Claude Code (cache dated 2026-06-24) and must be re-verified. (c) Reused from sibling sweeps in this project (URLs returned HTTP 200 in src/links.tsv; facts per their summaries): claude.com 1M GA blog, Claude compaction docs, Claude context-management blog, Claude Code docs, OpenAI compaction / prompt-caching / conversation-state guides, Gemini caching docs, Google implicit-caching blog, FastML Llama 4 critique; openai.com/index/gpt-4-1 returned 403 in that check. UNKNOWN / NOT CONFIRMED: GPT-5.x API window (272K input / 400K total / 128K output), ChatGPT per-plan context (32K/128K/196K), OpenAI's stated reason for defaults, DeepSeek V4 context (128K?) and MLA details, Mistral windows, Gemini 3 Pro exact window (1M vs 2M) and whether 3.x Pro keeps the 200K tier split, Anthropic's historical >200K premium pricing. VENDOR-STATED REASONS FOR CAPS found: Google frames it as cost/latency/retrieval-accuracy tradeoff (TTFT grows with length; multi-needle accuracy drops; caching ~4x cheaper). Magic quantifies KV-cache memory (638 H100s per user for a 100M-token KV cache on Llama 3.1 405B). Qwen quantifies serving memory (120-320 GB VRAM per 1M-token request) and relies on sparse attention for 3.2-6.7x prefill speedup. Meta shows 10M is extrapolation from 256K training, and independent tests show steep degradation. Pricing tiers encode serving cost: Gemini 2.5 Pro 2x input / 1.5x output above 200K; every Grok model 2x at >=200K; Anthropic removed its surcharge at 1M GA (March 2026). Default-vs-max: Claude Code product defaults to 200K while API models list 1M; Fable 5 makes 1M the default. HOW VENDORS EXTEND OR SIDESTEP: progressive RoPE-base context extension + Dual Chunk Attention extrapolation (Qwen); iRoPE interleaved no-PE layers + attention temperature scaling (Meta); non-attention sequence mechanism (Magic); and on the serving side, prefix/context caching (OpenAI 0.1x, Gemini ~10%, per-hour storage fees), server-side compaction (Anthropic default trigger 150K; OpenAI compact_threshold, Feb 2026), context editing and memory tools (Anthropic, +39%), server-held conversation state (OpenAI previous_response_id), deferred tool loading and subagents with separate windows (Claude Code).
